{{1980 Summer Olympics}}

The [[1980 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XXII Olympiad, were an international [[multi-sport event]] held in Moscow, [[Russian SFSR]], [[Soviet Union]], from 19 July to 3 August.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 Olympic Games {{!}} Boycott, Cold War, USSR, & Summer Games |url=https://www.britannica.com/event/Moscow-1980-Olympic-Games |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |date=2025-01-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820205959/https://www.britannica.com/event/Moscow-1980-Olympic-Games |archive-date=2022-08-20 |url-status=live |access-date=15 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Moscow 1980 IOC">{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=8 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220408132625/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980 |url-status=live }}</ref> They were the first Olympic Games to be staged in a communist nation.<ref name="RFERL">{{cite web |title=The 1980 Olympics Are The 'Cleanest' In History. Athletes Recall How Moscow Cheated The System. |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/the-1980-moscow-olympics-rank-as-the-cleanest-in-history-athletes-recall-how-the-u-s-s-r-cheated-the-system-/30741567.html |website=[[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]] |date=2020-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231094845/https://www.rferl.org/amp/the-1980-moscow-olympics-rank-as-the-cleanest-in-history-athletes-recall-how-the-u-s-s-r-cheated-the-system-/30741567.html |archive-date=2022-12-31 |url-status=live |last1=Aleksandrov |first1=Aleksei |last2=Grebeniuk |first2=Ivan |last3=Runets |first3=Volodymyr |last4=Scollon |first4=Michael |access-date=31 December 2022}}</ref> A total of 5,179 athletes representing 80 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated,<ref name="Moscow 1980 IOC" /> which included seven teams making their Olympic debut at the Summer Games; [[Angola at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Angola]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Angola – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/angola |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042451/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/angola |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> [[Botswana at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Botswana]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Botswana – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/botswana |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042619/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/botswana |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> [[Cyprus at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Cyprus]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Cyprus – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/cyprus |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250105031226/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/cyprus |archive-date=5 January 2025 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> [[Jordan at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Jordan]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Jordan – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/Jordan |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241224141518/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/jordan |archive-date=24 December 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=20 January 2025}}</ref> [[Laos at |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006043628/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/lao-pdr |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> [[Mozambique at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Mozambique]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Mozambique – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/mozambique |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130182315/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/mozambique |archive-date=30 November 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> and [[Seychelles at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Seychelles]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Seychelles – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/seychelles |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006044906/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/seychelles |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref> This was the smallest number of participating NOCs since [[1956 Summer Olympics|1956]].<ref name="Moscow 1980 IOC" /> The games featured 203 events in 21 [[Olympic sports|sports]] across 27 disciplines.<ref name="Moscow 1980 IOC" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lorge |first=Barry |date=1980-07-19 |title=Moscow's Moment |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1980/07/19/moscows-moment/ef3c21a4-8cfd-4d74-b636-444ab35ed350/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219204501/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1980/07/19/moscows-moment/ef3c21a4-8cfd-4d74-b636-444ab35ed350/ |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=19 February 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=When Fosbury turned his 'flop' into a big hit |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/rio-2016-olympics/olympics-history/when-fosburys-flop-produced-a-hit/article8912406.ece |website=[[The Hindu]] |date=2016-07-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622041832/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/rio-2016-olympics/olympics-history/when-fosburys-flop-produced-a-hit/article8912406.ece |archive-date=2024-06-22 |url-status=live |last1=Rao |first1=Rakesh |access-date=19 February 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

67 eligible countries participated in a [[1980 Summer Olympics boycott|boycott]] against these games, some of which did so explicitly citing the [[Soviet invasion of Afghanistan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980: Forty years on |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/moscow-1980-forty-years-on |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=20 January 2025 |date=19 July 2020 |archive-date=16 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816041553/https://olympics.com/en/news/moscow-1980-forty-years-on |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cold War rivalries split the Olympics in Moscow in 1980 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-virus-outbreak-afghanistan-boycotts-cold-war-8b447c53e96621f1ca2b06e8621b351f |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=2020-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240523085521/https://apnews.com/article/sports-virus-outbreak-afghanistan-boycotts-cold-war-8b447c53e96621f1ca2b06e8621b351f |archive-date=2024-05-23 |url-status=live |last1=Ellingworth |first1=James |access-date=20 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Sixteen NOCs participated under the [[Olympic Flag]], as opposed to their nation's flag, as a partial boycott.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Smith |first=Stephen |author-link=Stephen G. Smith (writer) |date=4 August 1980 |title=Olympics: Cheers, Jeers in Moscow |url=https://time.com/archive/6854777/olympics-cheersjeers-in-moscow/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125170324/https://time.com/archive/6854777/olympics-cheersjeers-in-moscow/ |archive-date=25 January 2025 |access-date=2025-02-19 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time ]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Fimrite |first=Ron |author-link=Ron Fimrite |date=28 July 1980 |title=Only The Bears Were Bullish |url=https://vault.si.com/vault/1980/07/28/only-the-bears-were-bullish-the-glittering-opening-ceremony-of-the-moscow-olympics-was-tarnished-by-the-62-nation-boycott-symbolic-protests-of-16-participating-countries-and-bad-vibes-in-the-village |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007154049/https://vault.si.com/vault/1980/07/28/only-the-bears-were-bullish-the-glittering-opening-ceremony-of-the-moscow-olympics-was-tarnished-by-the-62-nation-boycott-symbolic-protests-of-16-participating-countries-and-bad-vibes-in-the-village |archive-date=7 October 2022 |access-date=20 January 2025 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-us}}</ref> This included the [[Olympic Hymn|Olympic Anthem]] and flag being used at medal ceremonies when athletes from these NOCs won medals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stars and Stripes To Fly at Games Despite U.S. Ban |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1980/07/16/stars-and-stripes-to-fly-at-games-despite-us-ban/f5f3d653-3afc-490d-899f-9d429f8b7eee/?utm_term=.bb009affacdd |date=1980-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126000113/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1980/07/16/stars-and-stripes-to-fly-at-games-despite-us-ban/f5f3d653-3afc-490d-899f-9d429f8b7eee/ |archive-date=2025-01-26 |url-status=live |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |last1=Lorge |first1=Barry |url-access=subscription |access-date=20 January 2025}}</ref>

Athletes representing 36 NOCs received at least one medal, with 25 NOCs winning at least one gold medal.<ref name="IOC medal table" /> The [[Soviet Union at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Soviet Union]] won the most overall medals, with 195, and the most gold medals, with 80, setting a new record for most golds won in a single games (which was later broken at the [[1984 Summer Olympics|1984 Games]]).<ref name="IOC medal table" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Which Countries Have Won the Most Olympic Medals? |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/which-countries-have-won-the-most-olympic-medals/1147903/ |website=[[NBC Sports]] |date=2022-02-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803012812/https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/which-countries-have-won-the-most-olympic-medals/1147903/ |archive-date=2024-08-03 |url-status=live |last1=Murphy |first1=Bryan |access-date=20 January 2025}}</ref> Sports commentators noted that the absence of the [[United States at the Summer Olympics|United States]] and various other [[Western world|Western]] nations stemming from a large-scale boycott contributed to the highly skewed medal results benefitting the Soviet Union.<ref name="RFERL" /> [[Guyana at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Guyana]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Guyana – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/guyana |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006043337/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/guyana |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref> [[Tanzania at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Tanzania]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Tanzania – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/tanzania |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006044606/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/tanzania |archive-date=6 October 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref> and [[Zimbabwe at the 1980 Summer Olympics|Zimbabwe]] won their first Olympic medals of any kind, with Zimbabwe also winning their nation's first gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zimbabwe – Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/zimbabwe |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211001832/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/zimbabwe |archive-date=11 December 2024 |url-status=dead |access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref>

Among individual participants, Soviet gymnast [[Alexander Dityatin]] won the most medals overall with eight medals (three gold, four silver, one bronze), becoming the first athlete to win eight medals at a single games.<ref name="Olympedia medal table">{{Cite web |title=1980 Moskva Summer Games |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1980/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417041813/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/1980/ |archive-date=2020-04-17 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref name="uk">{{cite web |title=British Olympic Association: Moscow 1980 |url=http://www.olympics.org.uk/gamesabout.aspx?gt=s&ga=20 |website=[[British Olympic Association]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100428124938/http://www.olympics.org.uk/gamesabout.aspx?gt=s&ga=20 |archive-date=28 April 2010 |url-status=dead |access-date=20 August 2010}}</ref> Dityatin, Soviet canoer [[Vladimir Parfenovich]], Soviet swimmer [[Vladimir Salnikov]], and East German swimmers [[Barbara Krause]], [[Caren Metschuck]], and [[Rica Reinisch]] tied for the most gold medals, with three each.<ref name="Olympedia medal table" />

==Medal table==
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-W0727-138, Moskau, Olympiade, Siegerinnen über 200 m Rücken.jpg|thumb|alt=Black and white image showing three women with their Olympic medals.|East Germany swept the podium in the [[Swimming at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's 200 metre backstroke|women's 200 metre backstroke]] at the 1980 Summer Games.<ref>{{cite web |title=200 metres Backstroke, Women |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/6895 |website=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=17 January 2025 |archive-date=2 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502085112/http://www.olympedia.org/results/6895 |url-status=live }}</ref> From left to right: [[Cornelia Polit]], [[Rica Reinisch]], and [[Birgit Treiber]].]]
{{see also|Olympic medal table}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |work=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |work=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>

Events in [[Boxing at the 1980 Summer Olympics|boxing]] resulted in bronze medals being awarded to each of the competitors who lost their semi-final matches, as opposed to them taking part in a [[Third place playoff|third place tiebreaker]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Explained: Two bronze medals are awarded in the Olympics boxing competition |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=1 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328143327/https://olympics.com/en/news/why-two-bronze-medals-boxing |archive-date=28 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Ansari |first1=Aarish |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref> Events in [[Judo at the 1980 Summer Olympics|judo]] used a [[repechage system]] which also resulted in two bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Repechage in wrestling and other sports explained – the second chance |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] | date=21 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240802015913/https://olympics.com/en/news/what-is-repechage-rules |archive-date=2 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Nag |first1=Utathya |access-date=2 August 2024 }}</ref>

In [[Gymnastics at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's floor|women's gymnastics floor]] there were two-way ties for first and third, respectively, resulting in two gold medals and two bronze medals being issued, with no silver medal being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 floor exercises women Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/floor-exercises-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=2 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002205329/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/floor-exercises-women |url-status=live }}</ref> In [[Athletics at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Men's pole vault|men's pole vault]] and the [[Gymnastics at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's artistic individual all-around|women's gymnastic artistic individual all-around]] events there were two-way ties for second, which resulted in two silver medals and no bronze medals being awarded in each event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 pole vault men men Results – Olympic athletics |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/athletics/pole-vault-men |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127123809/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/athletics/pole-vault-men |archive-date=2024-11-27 |url-status=live |access-date=15 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 individual all-round women Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/individual-all-round-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=2 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002205325/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/individual-all-round-women |url-status=live }}</ref> Lastly, in the [[Gymnastics at the 1980 Summer Olympics – Women's uneven bars|women's uneven bars]], there was a three-way tie for third, which resulted in three bronze medals being awarded.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moscow 1980 uneven bars women Results – Olympic gymnastics-artistic |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/uneven-bars-women |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=2 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002205318/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/moscow-1980/results/gymnastics-artistic/uneven-bars-women |url-status=live }}</ref>
